DoLS Renewal Tracking Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Flagging window widened from 6 to 10 weeks to allow more time for local authority processing.*

Tracking

The registered manager reviews the DoLS tracker monthly and flags any authorisation expiring within 10 weeks (widened from 6 weeks) to the local authority.

Register controls

The site register records the authorisation reference, restrictions, conditions, start and expiry dates, representative, review events and renewal status for each resident. The registered manager reconciles the register with current authorisation documents monthly. A missing document, inconsistent date or unrecorded condition is investigated immediately rather than assumed to be an administrative delay.

Renewal workflow

Preparation starts far enough ahead to gather the current care plan, capacity assessment, restrictions and evidence of less restrictive alternatives. The application date, receiving authority and acknowledgement are recorded. Staff continue to follow the current lawful conditions while a renewal is considered and seek advice promptly where authority may expire before a decision.

Escalation and evidence

An approaching expiry without acknowledgement, a changed restriction or a condition that cannot be met is escalated to the registered manager and governance lead. The resident and representative are kept informed through the appropriate route. Applications, decisions, correspondence, reviews and escalation records are retained together so the authority position at any date can be reconstructed.

DBS Renewal Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2024. Single substantive change: 'may register' becomes 'must
register' with the DBS Update Service.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how an enhanced DBS check is renewed for a staff member at Alderbridge Care
Group. It applies to every role requiring an enhanced DBS check.

Policy statement

Enhanced DBS checks are renewed every 3 years, and staff must register with the DBS Update Service to
allow faster status checks between renewals — this is now a requirement, not an option — supporting both
regulatory compliance and administrative efficiency.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the detailed criminal record and barring check required for a role involving
regulated activity with a vulnerable adult. **DBS Update Service** the subscription service allowing a DBS
certificate's status to be checked online rather than a fresh application, saving time on onward checks,
registration with which is now mandatory. **Renewal cycle** the 3-year interval at which a full check is
renewed.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** tracks every staff member's DBS renewal date and DBS Update Service registration, notifying the
registered manager 8 weeks before expiry. **The registered manager** ensures the renewal application is
submitted in good time and confirms DBS Update Service registration for every staff member requiring an
enhanced check. **The staff member** completes the renewal application promptly when asked and must
register with the DBS Update Service.

1. Renew an enhanced DBS check every 3 years for every role requiring one.

2. HR notifies the registered manager 8 weeks before a certificate is due to expire, allowing time for the
renewal application to be completed.

3. Staff must register with the DBS Update Service; this is now mandatory rather than optional as under
the previous version.

4. Restrict a staff member from regulated activity if their DBS check lapses without a renewal in progress,
until it is resolved.

CQC Notification Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 August 2024. Adds a mandatory Quality Lead dual-review of every
notification before submission, and shortens the DoLS outcome notification timeframe from the previous
authorisation-linked window to within 3 working days of the outcome being known.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group notifies the Care Quality Commission of a notifiable
event. It applies to every site and covers events including a resident's death, a serious injury, an allegation
of abuse, a Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards outcome, and any event affecting the service's ability to
operate.

Policy statement

A notifiable event is reported to CQC accurately and within the required timeframe every time, since CQC's
own oversight depends on receiving a complete, honest picture of significant events across the service
rather than only those a provider chooses to disclose.

Definitions

**Notifiable event** an event CQC requires a provider to report under the relevant regulations, including
death, serious injury, abuse allegation, and DoLS outcome. **CQC online portal** the system used to
submit a notification directly to CQC. **Dual review** the mandatory second check by the Quality Lead of a
draft notification before it is submitted, now required for every notification regardless of category.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** identifies whether an event is notifiable and drafts the notification for
submission via the CQC online portal. **The Alderbridge Quality Lead** now reviews every draft
notification before submission, a new mandatory step, in addition to advising on borderline
notifiable-threshold cases. **Site staff** report any potentially notifiable event to the registered manager
immediately, rather than judging themselves whether it meets the threshold.

1. Identify whether an event meets a notifiable category as soon as it becomes known, escalating an
unclear case to the Quality Lead rather than deciding not to notify.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the removed same-day allowance. A prospective resident's family requests

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the same-day allowance removed for non-emergency cases?** A review found that proceeding
without the full GP summary occasionally missed a clinical detail that changed the admission decision;
requiring the summary first, except in a genuine emergency, closes that gap. **What does the new mental
capacity screen actually assess?** It is an initial, structured check of whether the prospective resident
appears to have capacity relevant to their admission and care decisions, feeding into but not replacing any
fuller capacity assessment needed later.

years, updated to cover the mental capacity screen and the narrowed emergency placement route.

Completed assessments and admission outcomes are reviewed monthly by the Quality Lead, including
specific attention to emergency placement route usage and mental capacity screen completion rates.

Record keeping and retention

Pre-admission assessments, including the mental capacity screen outcome, are retained in the resident's
care record per the Records Retention Schedule.

This policy works alongside the Safe Administration of Medication Policy and Controlled Drugs Procedure
(governing staff-administered medication generally) and the Mental Capacity Act guidance (governing how
the capacity element of the assessment is conducted).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the removed exemption. A resident wishes to apply their own daily
moisturising cream, prescribed for a skin condition. Under this version, this now requires the same full
capacity and risk assessment as any other self-administered medication before it begins, whereas the
previous version allowed this without a full assessment given its topical, low-risk nature.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the topical exemption removed?** A review found a small number of topical medications
carried a meaningful risk, such as an interaction or an application error, that the exemption had not
accounted for; assessing every category consistently closes that gap. **How is the quarterly re-review
different from the annual review?** It is a lighter-touch check confirming nothing has changed since the
last full review, rather than repeating the complete assessment four times a year.

Training and competency

Registered managers complete self-administration assessment training, refreshed every two years,
updated to cover the removed topical exemption and the new quarterly re-review, and care staff receive an
overview of the arrangement as part of medication awareness training.

Monitoring and compliance

Active self-administration arrangements and both their annual and quarterly review dates are tracked on
the site's medication register, reviewed monthly by the registered manager.

Record keeping and retention

Capacity and risk assessments and their outcomes, including each quarterly re-review, are retained per
the Records Retention Schedule alongside the resident's wider care record.

Approval and review history

These guidance notes were originally approved by the Chief Executive on 1 July 2025 and are scheduled for their next full review on 1 July 2026.

Appendix: the two-stage test explained

This appendix explains the Act's own two-stage test in more practical detail. Stage one asks whether the person has an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain, whether permanent or temporary — this alone does not determine incapacity, only whether the second stage needs to be considered at all. Stage two asks whether that impairment means the person cannot, at the time the decision needs to be made, understand relevant information about the decision, retain that information long enough to use it, weigh it up as part of the decision-making process, or communicate their decision by any means. A person lacks capacity for the specific decision only if stage one applies and they fail any one part of stage two — both stages genuinely matter, and staff are trained not to skip from 'has a diagnosis' straight to 'lacks capacity' without properly working through stage two.

Working with family members who hold Lasting Power of Attorney

Where a family member holds a registered Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare, or for property and financial affairs, staff confirm the specific scope of that authority before relying on it, since an attorney's authority is decision-specific to the type of LPA registered and does not automatically extend to every decision about the person, and Alderbridge keeps a copy of the registered document on file rather than relying on the family member's own description of their authority.

When a decision genuinely cannot wait

For a decision that must be made urgently and there is no attorney or existing best interests decision in place, the treating professional or care team makes the decision in the person's best interests using the information available at that moment, records the reasoning fully as soon as practicable afterward, and reviews it with fuller information once the urgency has passed, since acting reasonably with incomplete information in a genuine emergency is preferable to delaying necessary care while a more complete process is followed.

separate duty to notify the local authority safeguarding team or the police; the registered manager confirms
which additional bodies apply alongside the CQC notification, since a CQC notification alone does not

Notifying a change affecting service operation

A notifiable event also includes a significant change to the service's own ability to operate, such as a
prolonged loss of a key utility or a serious staffing shortfall genuinely affecting resident safety; this
category also now passes through the same dual-review step as any other notification before submission.

Handling a notification concerning a former resident

Where an event concerns a resident who has since left the service or been discharged, but the event
relates to care provided while they were resident, the same notification duty, timeframe and dual-review
requirement applies as if they remained in the service, since the obligation is tied to when the event
occurred, not to the resident's current status.

Closing note

Consistent, timely notification is one of the clearest ways a provider demonstrates it is being open with its
regulator, and the dual-review step in this version exists to make that standard more reliable without
slowing down the timeframe CQC itself requires.

Approval and review history

This overarching policy was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 March 2025, this version took effect 1 January 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in January 2027.

How the suite is kept up to date

A specific safeguarding procedure is reviewed on its own cycle, but any change is also checked against this overarching document, its appendices, and current terminology to confirm consistency across the whole suite.

Recognising self-neglect in practice

Self-neglect can present as declining personal hygiene support, an unwillingness to accept help with a deteriorating living space within the resident's own room, refusing food or fluids to a degree affecting health, or declining necessary medical treatment; staff are trained to notice these patterns and raise them, rather than dismissing them as simply 'the resident's choice' without the fuller Self-Neglect Guidance process being followed to properly weigh autonomy against risk.

Balancing autonomy and duty of care in self-neglect

The Self-Neglect Guidance requires a documented capacity assessment specific to the decision in question, since a resident may have capacity to decide about one aspect of their care while lacking it for another; where capacity is confirmed, the resident's own informed choice is respected and support is offered without being imposed, with the situation monitored and revisited periodically rather than treated as permanently settled.

Coordinating multi-agency information sharing in practice

Where a safeguarding concern involves another organisation, such as a domiciliary care provider a resident used before moving to Alderbridge, or a hospital involved in a recent admission, the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead coordinates what information is shared and requested, following the proportionality principle in the appendix rather than either withholding relevant information unhelpfully or sharing more than the situation genuinely requires.

Safeguarding Adults Board engagement

Alderbridge participates in the relevant local authority's Safeguarding Adults Board where a site's residents fall within that authority's area, contributing to multi-agency learning and receiving updates on local safeguarding priorities; the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead represents Alderbridge at this Board.

Dignity in Care Audit Procedure

SCHEDULED successor to the version effective 1 May 2025. Not yet effective; becomes authoritative on 1
November 2026, increasing audit frequency to monthly.

Audit frequency

A dignity in care audit will be carried out monthly (increased from quarterly) at each site using the standard
observation checklist, from 1 November 2026.

Audit preparation

The auditor samples different times, locations and care interactions and checks prior actions before
observation begins. Residents are told the purpose in an accessible way and may decline involvement.
The audit tool covers privacy, choice, communication, personal presentation, mealtime support,
confidential records and the physical environment rather than relying on a single general impression.

Evidence and escalation

Findings cite the observed or recorded evidence and distinguish an isolated lapse from a repeated or
systemic concern. Immediate risk, degrading treatment or possible abuse is escalated at once through
safeguarding and management routes; it is not left as a routine audit action. Positive practice is recorded
specifically enough to be repeated elsewhere.

Action and follow-up

Each shortfall receives an accountable owner, due date and completion evidence. The registered manager
reviews the action plan with residents or representatives where appropriate. Follow-up tests whether
practice changed in reality, and overdue or ineffective actions are escalated to the Quality Lead. Audit
tools, evidence, responses and closure decisions form one retained record.

candidates.text:
Update Service registration status, escalating an
approaching or lapsed renewal, or a missing registration, to the relevant registered manager.

Record keeping and retention

DBS renewal records, including DBS Update Service registration confirmation, are retained per the
Records Retention Schedule, held securely given their sensitive nature.

Approval and review history

This procedure was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 June 2024 and this version took effect,
superseding the earlier optional wording.

Handling a disclosed conviction on renewal

Where a renewal check discloses a new conviction or caution since the previous check, HR and the
registered manager assess it against the role's specific requirements and relevant guidance before
deciding on any action, rather than an automatic assumption that any new disclosure ends the person's
employment regardless of its relevance.

Renewal for a staff member changing role

Where a staff member moves from a role not requiring an enhanced DBS check into one that does, a fresh
check is initiated at that point rather than waiting for what would have been their next scheduled renewal
date under a role that never required one in the first place.

Cost of the renewal application

Alderbridge meets the cost of a DBS renewal application in full for a permanent staff member, since asking
staff to fund a mandatory employment requirement themselves would be an unreasonable barrier to
completing something the role genuinely requires.

A well-tracked renewal cycle protects residents by keeping every relevant check current, and mandatory
DBS Update Service registration in this version exists to make status verification faster and more
consistent for every staff member.

candidates.title: Dignity in Care Audit Procedure
candidates.text:
Dignity in Care Audit Procedure

SCHEDULED successor to the version effective 1 May 2025. Not yet effective; becomes authoritative on 1
November 2026, increasing audit frequency to monthly.

Audit frequency

A dignity in care audit will be carried out monthly (increased from quarterly) at each site using the standard
observation checklist, from 1 November 2026.

Audit preparation

The auditor samples different times, locations and care interactions and checks prior actions before
observation begins. Residents are told the purpose in an accessible way and may decline involvement.
The audit tool covers privacy, choice, communication, personal presentation, mealtime support,
confidential records and the physical environment rather than relying on a single general impression.

Evidence and escalation

Findings cite the observed or recorded evidence and distinguish an isolated lapse from a repeated or
systemic concern. Immediate risk, degrading treatment or possible abuse is escalated at once through
safeguarding and management routes; it is not left as a routine audit action. Positive practice is recorded
specifically enough to be repeated elsewhere.

Action and follow-up

Each shortfall receives an accountable owner, due date and completion evidence. The registered manager
reviews the action plan with residents or representatives where appropriate. Follow-up tests whether
practice changed in reality, and overdue or ineffective actions are escalated to the Quality Lead. Audit
tools, evidence, responses and closure decisions form one retained record.

candidates.title: Self-Administration of Medication Policy
candidates.text:
coincide with a routine visit where practicable.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Safe Administration of Medication Policy and Controlled Drugs Procedure
(governing staff-administered medication generally) and the Mental Capacity Act guidance (governing how
the capacity element of the assessment is conducted).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the removed exemption. A resident wishes to apply their own daily
moisturising cream, prescribed for a skin condition. Under this version, this now requires the same full
capacity and risk assessment as any other self-administered medication before it begins, whereas the
previous version allowed this without a full assessment given its topical, low-risk nature.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the topical exemption removed?** A review found a small number of topical medications
carried a meaningful risk, such as an interaction or an application error, that the exemption had not
accounted for; assessing every category consistently closes that gap. **How is the quarterly re-review
different from the annual review?** It is a lighter-touch check confirming nothing has changed since the
last full review, rather than repeating the complete assessment four times a year.

Training and competency

Registered managers complete self-administration assessment training, refreshed every two years,
updated to cover the removed topical exemption and the new quarterly re-review, and care staff receive an
overview of the arrangement as part of medication awareness training.

Monitoring and compliance

Active self-administration arrangements and both their annual and quarterly review dates are tracked on
the site's medication register, reviewed monthly by the registered manager.

Record keeping and retention

Capacity and risk assessments and their outcomes, including each quarterly re-review, are retained per
the Records Retention Schedule alongside the resident's wider care record

DoLS Renewal Tracking Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Flagging window widened from 6 to 10 weeks to allow more time for local authority processing.*

Tracking

The registered manager reviews the DoLS tracker monthly and flags any authorisation expiring within 10 weeks (widened from 6 weeks) to the local authority.

Register controls

The site register records the authorisation reference, restrictions, conditions, start and expiry dates, representative, review events and renewal status for each resident. The registered manager reconciles the register with current authorisation documents monthly. A missing document, inconsistent date or unrecorded condition is investigated immediately rather than assumed to be an administrative delay.

Renewal workflow

Preparation starts far enough ahead to gather the current care plan, capacity assessment, restrictions and evidence of less restrictive alternatives. The application date, receiving authority and acknowledgement are recorded. Staff continue to follow the current lawful conditions while a renewal is considered and seek advice promptly where authority may expire before a decision.

Escalation and evidence

An approaching expiry without acknowledgement, a changed restriction or a condition that cannot be met is escalated to the registered manager and governance lead. The resident and representative are kept informed through the appropriate route. Applications, decisions, correspondence, reviews and escalation records are retained together so the authority position at any date can be reconstructed.

---

DoLS Renewal Tracking Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Flagging window widened from 6 to 10 weeks to allow more time for local authority processing.*

Tracking

The registered manager reviews the DoLS tracker monthly and flags any authorisation expiring within 10 weeks (widened from 6 weeks) to the local authority.

Register controls

The site register records the authorisation reference, restrictions, conditions, start and expiry dates, representative, review events and renewal status for each resident. The registered manager reconciles the register with current authorisation documents monthly. A missing document, inconsistent date or unrecorded condition is investigated immediately rather than assumed to be an administrative delay.

Renewal workflow

Preparation starts far enough ahead to gather the current care plan, capacity assessment, restrictions and evidence of less restrictive alternatives. The application date, receiving authority and acknowledgement are recorded. Staff continue to follow the current lawful conditions while a renewal is considered and seek advice promptly where authority may expire before a decision.

Escalation and evidence

An approaching expiry without acknowledgement, a changed restriction or a condition that cannot be met is escalated to the registered manager and governance lead. The resident and representative are kept informed through the appropriate route. Applications, decisions, correspondence, reviews and escalation records are retained together so the authority position at any date can be reconstructed.

evidence_needs.aspect: DoLS expiry before January 2026 How many weeks before a DoLS expiry should I flag the renewal now, compared with the rule before January 2026?

question_span.quote: How many weeks before a DoLS expiry should I flag the renewal now, compared with the rule before January 2026?

answer_parts.text: Now (current procedure), flag any authorisation expiring within 10 weeks to the local authority.
Before January 2026 (earlier version), flag any authorisation expiring within 6 weeks to the local authority.
